original_question: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be compact. The Steiner problem considered here is: find a closed set St of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(St)) such that St \cup A is connected; such a minimizer is called a Steiner set, and if St is connected it is called a Steiner tree (in particular, this holds when A is finite). For dimensions d \ge 3, does there exist a finite set of terminals A such that there are two different Steiner trees St_1 and St_2 connecting A, but the directions of all segments incident to terminals are the same (equivalently, the two trees coincide in a neighborhood of the terminals)?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem almost exactly: it uses the paper’s Steiner-set/Steiner-tree framework, the minimal-length objective \(\mathcal{H}^1\), the finite-terminal case, the dimension restriction \(d \ge 3\), and the key extra condition that two distinct Steiner trees have the same terminal-edge directions, equivalently that they coincide near the terminals.
missing_details: The paper asks the question only for a finite set of terminals \(A \subset \mathbb{R}^d\), not for a general compact set; the broader compact-set setup is background, not part of the official formulation.
The two objects must be two distinct Steiner trees for the same terminal set \(A\).
The dimension restriction \(d \ge 3\) is essential in the paper’s formulation, because the next sentence notes that the analogous phenomenon is impossible in the plane.
The phrase "segments incident to terminals" relies on the preceding structural context that the edges of a Steiner tree are straight line segments.
The paper explicitly treats "same directions of all segments incident to terminals" as equivalent to "the trees coincide in a neighborhood of the terminals."
refined_question: Let \(A \subset \mathbb{R}^d\) be a finite set of terminals, where \(d \ge 3\). A Steiner tree for \(A\) is a closed connected set \(T \subset \mathbb{R}^d\) of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure \(\mathcal{H}^1(T)\) among all closed sets \(S\) such that \(S \cup A\) is connected. Does there exist such a terminal set \(A\) for which there are two distinct Steiner trees \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) connecting \(A\), but the directions of all straight segments incident to the terminals are the same in \(T_1\) and \(T_2\); equivalently, \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) coincide in a neighborhood of every terminal?
equivalent_formulation: Does there exist a finite terminal set \(A \subset \mathbb{R}^d\), with \(d \ge 3\), that admits two distinct Steiner trees which coincide in a neighborhood of all terminals?
justification: This draft is already a very close paraphrase of the paper’s official open problem. The nearest exact target is Question 2.1 in Section 2.1. The only tightening needed is to remove the unnecessary general compact-set preamble and state the problem directly for finite terminal input, while retaining the Steiner-tree definition supplied at the start of Section 2. The same Section 2 setup provides the local straight-segment structure behind the phrase about directions at terminals, and Question 2.1 itself gives the equivalent reformulation in terms of coincidence near terminals. The sentence immediately following the question explains why the scope is restricted to \(d \ge 3\): the planar case is already known to be impossible.
